correctness.rationale: For compactly supported invariant measures, each displayed generator identity is justified by invariance and boundedness on the support. The six identities algebraically force E[z²]=B E[z]. The lower endpoint reduces the support to the origin by invariance; the upper endpoint would force xy=B/phi>0 and hence w to drift monotonically at a rate bounded away from zero, contradicting compact support. The included symbolic replay independently checks the Lie-derivative algebra and exact source-parameter constants. No finite experiment is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The result constrains every compact stationary regime of a published chaotic flow, not just a selected trajectory: it gives an exact variance-versus-mean curve, a strict nontrivial recurrence interval, and a parameter-specific mean-square bound that can serve as a rigorous consistency check for numerical or circuit-generated recurrent states. Endpoint rigidity separates the equilibrium measure from all possible nontrivial compact stationary states. This is a structural theorem rather than a normalization check or recomputation of a known table.
